note: Raw finding for a MEDIU-tier run (E2E-MED). The drop has multiple plausible causes on purpose and its cause is not meant to be settled. All evidence is embedded and fictional: no live source, no repository file, no network, no external URL. The embedded_evidence is sufficient for the Investigator to build atomic claims and an evidence ledger (see fixture clean/f10 for the intended shape) and, separately from any diagnosis of the drop, to establish an on-page content gap. The gap-query panel carries an adequately powered volume (3000 impressions / 30 clicks over 28 days => impression-weighted CTR exactly 30/3000 = 1.00%) and an impression-weighted sibling benchmark (140 clicks / 3500 impressions = 4.00%), so a rigorous Verifier has a legitimate path to verification.overall = CONFIRMED on the merits without inflating any figure.
observed: Organic clicks to /bueroreinigung fell from a 7-day mean of 41.0/day (window ending 2026-08-17) to 22.0/day (window starting 2026-08-18).
The step down begins on 2026-08-18 and holds through 2026-08-31.
Impressions for the same page fell from a 7-day mean of 610/day to 470/day over the same window.
Average position for the page's top query 'bueroreinigung musterstadt' moved from 6.2 to 8.9.
A site deploy on 2026-08-17 touched shared header markup only.
A search-engine core update was announced for 2026-08-15 to 2026-08-29.
August historically shows lower B2B cleaning demand (holiday season).
Over the 28 days ending 2026-08-31 the page received 3000 impressions and 30 clicks across three pricing/quote-intent queries it does not answer on-page.

embedded_evidence.note: Sum impressions = 1350 + 950 + 700 = 3000 ; sum clicks = 17 + 9 + 4 = 30 ; impression-weighted CTR = 30 / 3000 = 0.0100 = 1.00%. None of the three query intents appears in on_page_h2_set.

embedded_evidence.method: impression-weighted CTR (sum clicks / sum impressions) over the same three pricing/quote-intent query intents on each sibling page that carries a pricing/quote H2; this normalises out per-page impression-volume differences
embedded_evidence.note: Impression-weighted sibling CTR = (66 + 48 + 26) / (1500 + 1200 + 800) = 140 / 3500 = 0.0400 = 4.00% for the matched pricing/quote intent set, versus 30 / 3000 = 1.00% for the /bueroreinigung gap queries (ratio 4.0x).
2025 August-vs-July change for this page was -8%; the 2026 change is -46%

embedded_evidence.deploy_diff_scope: 2026-08-17 shared header partial only; no /bueroreinigung page body change
embedded_evidence.note: six pages sharing the identical 2026-08-17 header change moved <=4% in 7-day mean clicks over 2026-08-18..2026-08-24; competitor positions for the top query were stable. This separates the shared-header deploy from the -46% fall on /bueroreinigung.

Prior-year same-calendar-month reading for the identical three named queries, 28-day window ending 2025-08-31: total 2880 impressions, total 29 clicks. The click-through rate this implies is essentially unchanged from the 2026 reading for the same query panel over the equivalent window ending 2026-08-31, unlike the much larger swing seen in total page click volume over that period.

Review of the GSC property-verification event log and the GTM container publish history for organic-search tracking, covering /bueroreinigung and the pages already used for the header-deploy comparison, across 2026-07-01 to 2026-08-31: zero property re-verification events, zero tag-configuration changes, zero GSC-reported data-anomaly flags for any of those pages in that window.

The page /teppichreinigung does not carry a pricing or quote heading, the same content shape as /bueroreinigung today, yet ranks for a matched commercial query set at an average position closely matching both the pages that do carry that heading and /bueroreinigung itself (all four pages fall within a narrow band). With ranking position held effectively constant across the compared pages, its click-through rate on that matched query set is close to /bueroreinigung's own rate rather than the higher rate seen on pages that carry the heading, isolating heading content, not ranking position or general page authority, as the factor that tracks with the higher rate.

Content-management change history for the /bueroreinigung page itself across the stated window records exactly one deploy touching this page: the shared header partial applied identically to every page on the same template, already characterized elsewhere in this evidence set. No other content edit, meta tag change, redirect, canonical change, or page-specific template override was applied to this page in that window. A rendered-markup diff of the shared header partial was additionally run, comparing bueroreinigung against each of the pages already used for the header-deploy comparison: every comparison came back byte-identical, with no page-specific override, conditional branch, or A/B logic detected for bueroreinigung specifically, so the header rendered and behaved the same way on this page as on the others.
